items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I did get to meet Louis Bellson who I didn’t know, and Charlie Shavers, and Ziggy Elman.

ctx.x: Oh, okay. Oh Dorsey calling you a bad name. That’s what it was.

But it wasn’t really, I mean he called everybody — I mean what happened actually, now this was 1947. If I worked three days a year I was doing well. I was an unknown playing on 52nd Street once in a while, learning, trying to learn bebop like Charlie Parker. And I get a call from Tommy Dorsey’s office, would I join the Tommy Dorsey band. $165 a week. Now I was making $165 every two years. And so he would fly me out there, you know, everything first class. And my mother wouldn’t let me fly. And you’ve got to…
